cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

## Question and scope

Does the default CLI preserve Unicode, input column order, and CSV field
boundaries? The historical default at `fe6be697cf9b79f22e4e1cd419efd0b3d7d57281`
stripped non-ASCII characters and did not escape fields. The prepared change
selected the existing `full` implementation by default; that already fixed the
two original diagnostic cases. This review additionally fixes quoting for CR.
No historical natural-language policy failure is claimed: these are executable
component configurations, not model instructions or a policy experiment.
There are no model calls, token comparisons, or empty-policy control; `baseline`
is the executable control, not an empty-policy prompt.

## Observations

P = exact-output pass, F = functional serialization failure.

| Case | Historical default | Prepared default | Current default/full | Baseline | Without Unicode | Without escaping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unicode | F | P | P | F | F | P |
| escaping | F | P | P | F | P | F |
| column-order | P | P | P | P | P | P |
| carriage-return | F | F | P | F | P | F |
| combined | F | P | P | F | F | F |
| trailing-space | P | P | P | P | P | P |
| empty-row | P | P | P | P | P | P |
| coercion | P | P | P | P | P | P |

Unicode failures lose characters; escaping failures lose field boundaries or
quote syntax. The Unicode ablation removes preservation but retains escaping;
the escaping ablation removes quoting but retains Unicode. Shared mapping and
joining preserve order in all configurations. Ablation failures alone are not
proof of improvement over either historical or prepared defaults.

These are eight synthetic regression cases, not independent workload samples.
The two original cases are reused diagnostics. The added cases are regression
coverage, not held-out validation. Current default and explicit full are separate
invocations of the same implementation. No runtime errors occurred in the saved
56 program executions. Local tooling initially lacked Python; setup was repaired
using Node before this run. No model recovery or failure-exposure claim is made.

## Evidence and reproduction

Requires Node.js (recorded run: v22.23.4) and Git with the historical commit
available. No packages, credentials, network, or manual grading required.
From the repository root:

```sh
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/prepared-results.json
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/results.json
node eval/run.mjs --output .local/review-new.json
```

Use a new output filename on each fresh run (existing records are not overwritten).
Fresh runs read the current `app.mjs`; sources, hashes, cases and arguments are
frozen in memory before execution and saved with exact stdout, stderr, status and
runtime. Conditions are interleaved by case. The prepared candidate is generated
from the pinned historical artifact with only its default changed to `full`.
Infrastructure errors are recorded separately and fail the runner.

Grading is exact minimal CSV serialization with a single final LF; it intentionally
rejects equivalent all-quoted CSV. No stdout trimming or newline normalization is
allowed. Grader assertions cover correct, incorrect, equivalent-but-outside-contract,
nonzero exit, and whitespace-transformed output before executing candidates.

`prepared-results.json` is a safe allowlisted extract of the actual local capture:
inputs, outputs, scores, runtime and source hash are retained. Unrelated private
runtime context, local paths, authentication metadata and provider reasoning are
omitted and remain ignored. That old capture used `trimEnd`, so its replay only
verifies its original two scores; it cannot establish whitespace correctness.
`results.json` preserves the replacement measurement without overwriting those
superseded observations. Neither record contains provider data.
EOF

+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import crypto from 'node:crypto';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {spawnSync, execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
+
+process.chdir(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url)));
+const hash = text => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
+// Exact CSV serialization contract: UTF-8, minimal quoting, one final LF.
+// Never trim stdout: spaces, CR and LF can be field contents.
+const grade = (task, result) => result.status === 0 &&
+  result.stdout === task.expected + '\n';
+const probe = {expected: '"a,b",tail  '};
+assert(grade(probe, {status: 0, stdout: '"a,b",tail  \n'}));
+assert(!grade(probe, {status: 0, stdout: 'a,b,tail  \n'}));
+assert(!grade(probe, {status: 0, stdout: '"a,b",tail\n'}));
+assert(!grade(probe, {status: 1, stdout: '"a,b",tail  \n'}));
+// Quoting every field is semantically equivalent but outside this exact contract.
+assert(!grade(probe, {status: 0, stdout: '"a,b","tail  "\n'}));
+assert(!grade({expected: 'x\r'}, {status: 0, stdout: 'x\n'}));
+
+if (process.argv.includes('--replay')) {
+  const file = process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--replay') + 1];
+  const record = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
+  if (record.schema !== 1) {
+    // Legacy capture discarded trailing whitespace; only its two original
+    // cases can be replayed. Do not pretend that it captured raw stdout.
+    for (const row of record.results) {
+      const task = record.cases.find(t => t.id === row.case);
+      assert.equal(row.pass, row.actual === task.expected);
+    }
+    console.log(`Verified ${record.results.length} legacy scores (trimEnd limitation).`);
+  } else {
+    for (const row of record.results) {
+      const task = record.cases.find(t => t.id === row.case);
+      assert.equal(row.pass, grade(task, row));
+    }
+    console.log(`Verified ${record.results.length} exact-output scores.`);
+  }
+  process.exit(0);
+}
+
+// Freeze all executable candidates and inputs before executing any case.
+const revision = 'fe6be697cf9b79f22e4e1cd419efd0b3d7d57281';
+const historical = execFileSync('git', ['show', `${revision}:app.mjs`], {encoding:'utf8'});
+const current = fs.readFileSync('app.mjs', 'utf8');
+const cases = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('eval/cases.json', 'utf8'));
+const candidates = [
+  {id:'historical-default', source:historical, args:[]},
+  {id:'prepared-default', source:historical.replace("|| 'baseline'", "|| 'full'"), args:[]},
+  {id:'current-default', source:current, args:[]},
+  ...['baseline','full','without-unicode','without-escaping'].map(id =>
+    ({id, source:current, args:[id]})),
+];
+const results = [];
+for (const task of cases) {
+  for (const candidate of candidates) {
+    const result = spawnSync(process.execPath,
+      ['--input-type=module', '-e', candidate.source, '--', 'app.mjs',
+        JSON.stringify(task.input), ...candidate.args],
+      {encoding:'utf8', timeout:5000});
+    const row = {condition:candidate.id, case:task.id, status:result.status,
+      stdout:result.stdout, stderr:result.stderr,
+      infrastructureError:result.error?.message ?? null};
+    row.pass = grade(task, row);
+    results.push(row);
+    console.log(`${row.condition} / ${row.case}: ${row.infrastructureError ? 'INFRA' : row.pass ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}`);
+  }
+}
+const record = {schema:1, runtime:process.version, historicalRevision:revision,
+  cases, candidates:candidates.map(c => ({...c, sha256:hash(c.source)})), results};
+const outputIndex = process.argv.indexOf('--output');
+if (outputIndex !== -1) {
+  const output = process.argv[outputIndex + 1];
+  fs.writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + '\n', {flag:'wx'});
+}
+// Expected diagnostic failures do not make the run fail; production failures do.
+if (results.some(r => r.infrastructureError ||
+    (['current-default','full'].includes(r.condition) && !r.pass))) process.exitCode = 1;
